questions.question_text: Which WV license type allows the holder to operate independently and supervise salespersons?
questions.explanation: Only a broker can operate independently and supervise salespersons in WV. An associate broker holds broker qualifications but works under another broker, similar to a salesperson.

questions.question_text: How does an associate broker differ from a salesperson in West Virginia?
questions.explanation: An associate broker holds broker qualifications (education and experience) but chooses to work under another broker rather than operating independently. A salesperson has only salesperson-level qualifications.

questions.question_text: A newly licensed WV salesperson wants to practice real estate. What is required before they can begin?
questions.correct_answer: Must be sponsored by an employing broker
distractors: Must complete 30 days of training first
Must register with the county clerk
Can begin immediately upon passing the exam
questions.explanation: A WV salesperson must be sponsored by an employing broker to activate their license. They cannot practice independently — all salespersons must work under a licensed broker.

questions.question_text: An experienced agent who qualifies as a broker decides to continue working under another broker's supervision. What license type applies?
questions.explanation: An associate broker holds broker qualifications but works under another broker's supervision. This allows experienced agents to maintain broker credentials without the responsibilities of operating a brokerage.

questions.question_text: Which of the following accurately describes West Virginia's license structure?
distractors: Associate, designated broker, and principal broker
questions.explanation: WV has three license types: salesperson (works under broker), associate broker (broker-qualified but works under another broker), and broker (operates independently, supervises others).

questions.question_text: What is the application processing fee for a WV real estate license?
questions.explanation: The application processing fee is $25, paid through the WVREC Online Application System. Separately, there is a $45.75 fingerprint fee and a $75 license activation fee.

questions.question_text: A WV salesperson renews their license on time during the May 1–June 30 period. What is the renewal fee?
questions.explanation: The annual renewal fee for a WV salesperson is $75 (174-2-2.4.2); brokers and associate brokers pay $150. Renewing after the June 30 expiration adds a tiered late fee: $50 from July 1 through August 31, $75 from September 1 through October 31, and $100 from November 1 through December 31.

questions.question_text: Who processes the fingerprints a WV license applicant submits for the criminal history record check?
questions.correct_answer: The WV State Police and the FBI
distractors: Pearson VUE as part of exam registration
The county sheriff where the applicant resides
questions.explanation: Under §30-40-11(f)(2) and 174-1-5.1, fingerprints go to the West Virginia State Police, or its assigned agent, for a state check by the State Police's Criminal Identification Bureau and a national check by the FBI. The State Police currently use IdentoGO as the collecting agent; the applicant pays that vendor's actual costs, which are set by the vendor and not by the Commission's fee schedule.

questions.question_text: WV real estate license applications are submitted through which system?
questions.explanation: Applications can only be completed online through the WVREC Online Application System. Paper applications are no longer accepted.

questions.question_text: What is the license activation fee for a new WV salesperson?
questions.explanation: The salesperson license fee is $75 for the initial and any subsequent license (174-2-2.3.2), separate from the $25 application fee and the fingerprint vendor's charge. A broker or associate broker license fee is $150, as is a branch office license. The license is issued once the applicant has a sponsoring broker, and the fee must be paid within three months of passing the exam (174-1-4.7).

questions.question_text: How many clock hours of education are required for a WV broker license?
questions.explanation: A broker applicant must complete at least 180 clock-hours, equivalent to 12 college semester credit hours (§30-40-14(a)). An applicant who already holds a West Virginia salesperson's license satisfies this by completing an additional 90 clock-hours on top of the salesperson's 90 — 30 hours of Brokerage Operation and Management, 25 of Human Resources Management and Interpersonal Skills, and 35 of West Virginia-Specific Real Estate for Brokers.

questions.question_text: A salesperson with 12 closed transactions over the past 2 years wants to upgrade to a broker license. Do they meet the experience requirement on that basis?
questions.correct_answer: No, the two-year route requires 20 closed transactions
distractors: No, the two-year route requires 15 closed transactions
Yes, any 2 years of active licensure qualifies
questions.explanation: W. Va. Code §30-40-12(a)(1)(i) requires the applicant to show "real estate experience as a licensed real estate salesperson during the two years prior to the date of application showing the applicant's representation of a buyer or seller in a minimum of 20 closed transactions." Twelve is short of 20. The only alternative is 40 closed transactions regardless of the number of years licensed.

questions.question_text: A salesperson has completed 22 closed transactions over 5 years but only 8 in the last 2 years. Do they qualify for a broker license on experience?
questions.correct_answer: No, the career route requires 40 closed transactions
distractors: Yes, 20 or more total transactions qualifies
No, only transactions in the last 2 years ever count
Yes, five years of licensure alone qualifies
questions.explanation: Two routes are available and this applicant meets neither: 20 closed transactions during the two years before application (they have 8), or "regardless of the number of years as a licensed salesperson: a minimum of 40 closed transactions" (they have 22) — §30-40-12(a)(1). A "closed transaction" means real estate actually conveyed from seller to buyer with the applicant representing a side, or a consummated lease of at least one year.

questions.question_text: How many scored state-specific items are on the WV broker exam compared to the salesperson exam?
questions.explanation: The WV broker exam has 60 scored state-specific items compared to 50 for the salesperson exam. The broker exam includes an additional section on Broker Management (18 items).

questions.question_text: The WV broker exam includes an additional section not on the salesperson exam covering which topics?
questions.explanation: The broker exam includes a Broker Management section (18 items) covering trust funds, place of business, brokerage operations, and HR management — supervisory topics not tested on the salesperson exam.
